title: Japanese Travel & Conversation — Beginner Course
designPrinciples: Begin with an explicit learner goal and a short, familiar scene; assume no prior lesson or Japanese knowledge.
Conversation and listening are the goal; scripts and kanji support communication rather than delay it.
Dialogue and phrase text use kana-first Japanese. Do not require romaji; keep it as an optional temporary scaffold.
The three weekly lessons build from noticing meaning, to supported replies, to adapting a conversation.
Local speech, reading, a partner, or self-led practice are alternatives; speech setup never gates a lesson.
Completion records practice and observable evidence, never a claim of fluency or automated speech accuracy.

reviewCadence.sessionWarmup: Offer a low-pressure revisit only when an earlier lesson is marked practised. If there is no completed lesson, begin with the current goal and new material; never refer to a previous lesson that did not happen.
reviewCadence.weeklyInterleave: At the start of a later week, choose a phrase or line that appeared in a completed lesson from the previous week; if none was practised, teach the current scene instead.
reviewCadence.longerSpacing: Mix in an item from two to four weeks earlier only when a lesson from that week was completed and the item appeared in that lesson. Prefer learner-marked difficult items and change the scene.
reviewCadence.milestoneRevisit: At a checkpoint, invite one earlier conversation function only when it has been practised; keep the main checkpoint on the current milestone.
reviewCadence.adaptation: Introduce review cards after a lesson is completed or after the learner explicitly self-rates an item. First scheduled review is the following day; a missed item returns sooner, while an easy recall waits longer. Review stays optional and unscored.

learningPath.title: Find your first words
learningPath.outcome: Greet someone, introduce yourself, ask simple what/where questions, and request repetition when you miss something.

learningPath.title: Handle everyday needs
learningPath.outcome: Make a café or shop request, handle a simple transaction, and share preferences or food needs.

learningPath.title: Get around
learningPath.outcome: Ask for directions, follow a short route, make a simple plan, and confirm time and place.

learningPath.title: Keep the conversation moving
learningPath.outcome: Tell a short travel story, ask for help, handle a changed detail, and combine familiar exchanges with less scripting.

kanaPolicy: Every Japanese dialogue line and phrase is written in kana. Topic-specific kanji are shown separately with a kana reading and practical recognition goal. Script practice appears in the scene that uses it and never gates speaking or course progress.

weeks.title: Open a conversation
weeks.canDo: Greet someone, get their attention politely, thank them, and close a brief exchange.

phraseBank.ja: こんにちは。
すみません。
phraseBank.use: Get attention or make a brief apology.

phraseBank.ja: ありがとうございます。
お願いします。

kanaFocus: あいうえお
かきくけこ
さしすせそ
たちつてと

lessons.title: A polite first hello
lessons.goal: Return a simple greeting and use すみません to begin a polite request.
lessons.scene: You enter a small hotel. The receptionist welcomes you and asks a longer reservation question; today, focus on greeting them back and opening politely. You do not need to understand every word yet.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: こんにちは。いらっしゃいませ。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: こんにちは。

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: ごよやくのおなまえをおねがいします。
dialogue.en: May I have the name on the reservation?

listenCheck.question: Which greeting can you use to answer the receptionist?

responsePractice.prompt: The staff member says こんにちは. Choose a suitable reply.
responsePractice.why: A daytime greeting can be returned with the same greeting.

lessons.sayTask: Say a greeting, then say すみません to get the receptionist's attention.
lessons.adaptation: Change the hotel to a shop or station. Return the greeting, then use すみません to get the person’s attention.
successChecks: Chooses a polite greeting in return
Uses すみません to open a request

lessons.title: Thank and respond
lessons.goal: Ask where a useful place is, understand a short reply, and thank the helper.
lessons.scene: Someone at a station points you toward the ticket machines.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: すみません。きっぷうりばはどこですか。
dialogue.en: Excuse me. Where is the ticket counter?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: あちらです。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: ありがとうございます。

listenCheck.question: What does the traveller say after getting help?

responsePractice.prompt: Someone helps you and says nothing more. What is a polite response?
choices: ありがとうございます。
responsePractice.why: ありがとうございます is a polite way to show thanks.

lessons.sayTask: Practise the request with a partner. Take the traveller role and finish with thanks.
lessons.adaptation: Replace the ticket counter with a restroom, then repeat the exchange.

lessons.title: A small exchange, your way
lessons.goal: Respond to an offer and adapt your answer when the situation changes.
lessons.scene: A shop worker hands you a bag and checks whether you need anything else.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: ふくろをどうぞ。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: ありがとうございます。

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: ほかにごようけんはありますか。
dialogue.en: Is there anything else you need?

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: いいえ、だいじょうぶです。

listenCheck.question: Does the traveller need another item?

responsePractice.prompt: A staff member asks if you need anything else. You do not. Choose a polite reply.
choices: いいえ、だいじょうぶです。
responsePractice.why: This politely signals that you are fine and do not need more.

lessons.sayTask: Do a four-turn shop exchange without looking at the English meanings.
lessons.adaptation: Change the final answer so you do need one more item; ask for it politely.
successChecks: Understands whether help is being offered
Adds a changed detail without losing politeness

weeks.title: Introduce yourself
weeks.canDo: Give a short self-introduction, say where you are from, and answer a few simple personal questions.

phraseBank.ja: はじめまして。
わたしは [なまえ] です。
[くに] からきました。
よろしくおねがいします。
phraseBank.en: Pleased to meet you / I look forward to it.

kanaFocus: なにぬねの
はひふへほ
まみむめも
やゆよ
らりるれろ
わをん

kanjiCards.whyHere: A useful recognition character on signs and forms about people; no handwriting test.
A practical word likely to appear in an introduction or reservation form.

milestone.title: Introduction checkpoint
milestone.task: Give a 30-second self-introduction and answer three familiar personal questions. From five slow, clear questions, identify the key information in at least four.
evidence: Support used and next practice target

lessons.title: Hear a first introduction
lessons.goal: Introduce yourself with your name and a polite first-meeting closing.
lessons.scene: You meet another traveller at a guesthouse.

dialogue.speaker: travellerA
dialogue.ja: はじめまして。あきです。
dialogue.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Aki.

dialogue.speaker: travellerB
dialogue.ja: はじめまして。けんです。
dialogue.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Ken.

dialogue.speaker: travellerA
dialogue.ja: よろしくおねがいします。

listenCheck.question: What is traveller A's name?

responsePractice.prompt: You have just been introduced. Which line fits best?
responsePractice.why: はじめまして is used when meeting someone for the first time.

lessons.sayTask: Say はじめまして, your name, then よろしくおねがいします.
lessons.adaptation: Repeat with a different name and greet a second person.

lessons.title: Where are you from?
lessons.goal: Say where you are from and ask the same question back.
lessons.scene: A fellow guest asks where you came from.

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.ja: どちらからきましたか。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: オーストラリアからきました。

dialogue.speaker: guest
dialogue.ja: そうですか。

listenCheck.question: Which country does the traveller name?

responsePractice.prompt: Someone asks どちらからきましたか. Complete the answer with a place you choose.
responsePractice.why: The question asks about where you came from; name a place before からきました.

lessons.sayTask: Answer the question with your own country or city. Repeat once without the phrase bank.
lessons.adaptation: Ask the same question back after answering.
successChecks: Gives a place in the answer
Returns the question or adds a follow-up

lessons.title: Three simple questions
lessons.goal: Answer familiar personal questions and keep the exchange going with a follow-up.
lessons.scene: A host asks a visitor their name, country, and whether it is their first visit.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.ja: おなまえはなんですか。

dialogue.speaker: visitor
dialogue.ja: さきです。

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.ja: にほんははじめてですか。
dialogue.en: Is this your first time in Japan?

dialogue.speaker: visitor
dialogue.ja: はい、はじめてです。

listenCheck.question: Is this the visitor's first time in Japan?

responsePractice.prompt: Answer にほんははじめてですか truthfully.
choices: おすすめはなんですか。
responsePractice.why: This is a yes-answer to a question about a first visit.

lessons.sayTask: Complete the three-part checkpoint with your name, home country, and whether this is your first visit.
lessons.adaptation: Ask one of the questions to your partner, listen to the answer, and respond with そうですか or a follow-up.
successChecks: Answers at least two familiar questions
Can identify a name or place from a clear question
Keeps the exchange going with a follow-up

weeks.title: Ask, answer, and follow up
weeks.canDo: Ask what or where something is, ask for repetition, and respond to a simple answer.

phraseBank.ja: これはなんですか。
[ばしょ] はどこですか。
もういちどおねがいします。
ゆっくりおねがいします。

kanaFocus: がぎぐげご
ざじずぜぞ
だぢづでど
ばびぶべぼ
ぱぴぷぺぽ
きゃ・しゅ・ちょ

kanjiCards.whyHere: Recognize this common question character; the spoken reading changes with the phrase.

lessons.title: Ask what something is
lessons.goal: Ask what an unfamiliar item is and respond to the answer.
lessons.scene: You point to a small item on a café counter.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: すみません。これはなんですか。

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: ゆずのジュースです。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: そうですか。

listenCheck.question: What is the item?

responsePractice.prompt: You do not know what an item is. Choose the question.
choices: どちらからきましたか。
responsePractice.why: これはなんですか asks what the thing is.

lessons.sayTask: Point to an imagined item and ask これはなんですか. Listen to a partner's answer.
lessons.adaptation: Replace yuzu juice with one unfamiliar item and ask a second question about it.
successChecks: Uses これはなんですか

lessons.title: Ask where a place is
lessons.goal: Ask where a place is and understand a short location reply.
lessons.scene: You need to find the nearest restroom in a station.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: すみません。おてあらいはどこですか。
dialogue.en: Excuse me. Where is the restroom?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: あそこです。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: ありがとうございます。

listenCheck.question: Where is the restroom?

responsePractice.prompt: You need to locate the exit. Choose the useful question frame.
responsePractice.why: どこですか asks where something is.

lessons.sayTask: Ask where the restroom, exit, or ticket counter is; understand あそこ or こちら in reply.
lessons.adaptation: Swap the destination and ask for one more direction, such as upstairs or outside.

lessons.title: Ask for another listen
lessons.goal: Ask someone to repeat or slow down, then catch the key place or detail.
lessons.scene: A station announcement or helpful passer-by speaks too quickly.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: すみません。もういちどおねがいします。
dialogue.en: Excuse me. One more time, please.

dialogue.speaker: helper
dialogue.ja: えきは、あちらです。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: ゆっくりおねがいします。

listenCheck.question: Which place does the helper point to?

responsePractice.prompt: You missed an answer. Which repair phrase keeps the conversation going?
choices: もういちどおねがいします。
responsePractice.why: This politely asks the other person to repeat.

lessons.sayTask: Practise both repair phrases. Ask your partner to repeat and then to speak slowly.
lessons.adaptation: Listen once without text, use one repair phrase, and listen again before revealing the meaning.

weeks.title: Make a café request
weeks.canDo: Order a simple drink or item, ask for the price, and say whether you will eat in or take away.

phraseBank.ja: コーヒーをください。
メニューをおねがいします。
ここでたべます。
いくらですか。

kanaFocus: Hiragana review: small っ and long vowels
Katakana: アイウエオ・カキクケコ
Read menu words: コーヒー・メニュー

kanjiCards.whyHere: Recognize the currency character on a menu or price display.

milestone.title: Café and shop checkpoint
milestone.task: Complete a 60–90 second predictable café or shop exchange with a polite request and item confirmation. Catch the requested item or choice in four of five short prompts.
evidence: Support used and next practice target

lessons.title: Catch the order
lessons.goal: Order a familiar drink or item and answer a simple choice question.
lessons.scene: A café worker asks what you would like.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: ごちゅうもんは。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: コーヒーをください。

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: ホットですか、アイスですか。

listenCheck.question: What does the traveller order?

responsePractice.prompt: Order a coffee politely.
choices: コーヒーはどこですか。
コーヒーからきました。
responsePractice.why: ください makes a simple polite request.

lessons.sayTask: Order one drink and answer ホットですか、アイスですか with your preference.
lessons.adaptation: Replace coffee with tea or water and change hot/iced choice.

lessons.title: Eat here or take away
lessons.goal: Say whether you want to eat here or take your order away.
lessons.scene: The cashier asks whether the food is for here or to go.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: こちらでおめしあがりですか。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: はい、ここでたべます。

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: では、こちらでどうぞ。
dialogue.en: Then please have a seat here.

listenCheck.question: Where will the traveller eat?

responsePractice.prompt: You want to take the food away. Choose the response.
choices: もちかえりでおねがいします。
responsePractice.why: もちかえりでおねがいします requests takeaway.

lessons.sayTask: Answer the dine-in question once with yes and once with takeaway.
lessons.adaptation: Change the order from a drink to a sandwich; choose eat-in or take-away.

lessons.title: Confirm the price
lessons.goal: Understand a displayed or spoken price and make a choice.
lessons.scene: You are checking a menu before ordering at a counter.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: すみません。これはいくらですか。
dialogue.en: Excuse me. How much is this?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: ごひゃくえんです。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: では、これをください。

listenCheck.question: How much is the item?

responsePractice.prompt: You know what you want after hearing the price. What can you say?
choices: どちらからきましたか。
もういちどおねがいします。
responsePractice.why: では connects your decision to a polite order.

lessons.sayTask: Ask the price, listen to a number, then accept or politely choose another item.
lessons.adaptation: Use a different price and item. Ask the cashier to repeat if needed.
successChecks: Recognizes 円 on a price display
Makes a choice after hearing the answer

weeks.title: Shop for what you need
weeks.canDo: Ask for an item, specify a simple quantity, and handle a bag or payment question.

phraseBank.ja: これをひとつください。
ふたつください。
カードでおねがいします。
ふくろはいりますか。

kanaFocus: Katakana: サシスセソ・タチツテト
Katakana: ナニヌネノ・ハヒフヘホ
Read loanwords: サイズ・カード・レシート

kanjiCards.whyHere: Recognize a useful quantity form; practise saying the quantity, not handwriting the character.

lessons.title: Ask for an item
lessons.goal: Ask for a specific item and communicate a simple quantity.
lessons.scene: You need a bottle of water at a convenience store.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: みずをひとつください。

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: はい。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: ありがとうございます。

listenCheck.question: How many waters does the traveller ask for?

responsePractice.prompt: Ask for one item using a polite phrase.
choices: これをひとつください。
responsePractice.why: ひとつ gives the quantity and ください makes it a request.

lessons.sayTask: Choose a familiar shop item and order one. Then order two.
lessons.adaptation: Swap the item and quantity; say the whole request without the model.

lessons.title: Answer a checkout question
lessons.goal: Understand a bag question and accept or decline politely.
lessons.scene: At checkout, the worker asks if you need a bag.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: ふくろはいりますか。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: はい、おねがいします。

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: かしこまりました。

listenCheck.question: What does the traveller ask for?

responsePractice.prompt: You do not need a bag. Choose a short answer.
choices: いいえ、だいじょうぶです。
responsePractice.why: This politely declines the offer.

lessons.sayTask: Answer ふくろはいりますか both ways: yes and no.
lessons.adaptation: Add one more checkout detail, such as a receipt or payment method.
successChecks: Recognizes one checkout word in katakana

lessons.title: Pay and finish the purchase
lessons.goal: Pay for a small purchase and recover when a checkout detail changes.
lessons.scene: You have chosen two snacks and want to pay by card.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: おしはらいはどうしますか。
dialogue.en: How would you like to pay?

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: カードでおねがいします。

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: こちらにカードをおねがいします。
dialogue.en: Please tap or insert your card here.

listenCheck.question: How does the traveller pay?

responsePractice.prompt: The cashier asks how you will pay. Choose card.
choices: カードでおねがいします。
responsePractice.why: カード identifies card payment.

lessons.sayTask: Role-play an entire checkout: request an item, confirm the amount, answer about the bag, and pay.
lessons.adaptation: Change one detail unexpectedly (no bag, different quantity, or cash instead) and keep going.
successChecks: Recovers when one checkout detail changes

weeks.title: Preferences and recommendations
weeks.canDo: Say what you like or cannot eat, ask for a recommendation, and respond to a suggestion.

phraseBank.ja: おすすめはなんですか。
これがすきです。
あまいものがすきです。
phraseBank.use: Give a preference with a detail.

phraseBank.ja: [たべもの] のアレルギーがあります。たべられません。
phraseBank.en: I have an allergy to [food]. I can't eat it.
phraseBank.use: Name the specific allergy; show a written allergy card and have staff confirm ingredients and cross-contact risk.

kanaFocus: Katakana: マミムメモ・ヤユヨ・ラリルレロ
Katakana: ワ・ン・ー
Read food words: カレー・アイス・パン

kanjiCards.whyHere: A useful sign or menu word tied directly to preferences.

milestone.title: Preference and recommendation checkpoint
milestone.task: State a preference, ask for a recommendation, and add at least one follow-up. Identify the recommendation or choice in four of five clear replies.

lessons.title: Ask for a recommendation
lessons.goal: Ask what is recommended and add a relevant follow-up question.
lessons.scene: You are looking at a menu and ask the server what is popular.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: おすすめはなんですか。

dialogue.speaker: server
dialogue.ja: カレーがおすすめです。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: ありがとうございます。

listenCheck.question: What does the server recommend?

responsePractice.prompt: You want advice about what to order. Choose the question.
choices: おすすめはなんですか。
responsePractice.why: おすすめ asks for a recommendation.

lessons.sayTask: Ask for a recommendation and listen for one menu item.
lessons.adaptation: Ask whether the recommended item is spicy, hot, or sweet.

lessons.title: Say what you like
lessons.goal: Say which option you like and respond to a suggestion.
lessons.scene: A travelling companion asks which dessert you prefer.

dialogue.speaker: companion
dialogue.ja: あまいものはすきですか。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: はい、あまいものがすきです。

dialogue.speaker: companion
dialogue.ja: じゃあ、アイスクリームはどうですか。

listenCheck.question: What kind of food does the traveller like?

responsePractice.prompt: Say that you like curry.
responsePractice.why: がすきです is a beginner-friendly way to state a preference.

lessons.sayTask: State one food you like and one you do not like. Keep the answer simple.
lessons.adaptation: Respond to a suggestion with a yes or a polite no and a reason you choose.

lessons.title: Handle a food limitation
lessons.goal: Explain one food limitation and ask for or accept an alternative.
lessons.scene: You ask what is in a dish and explain that you cannot eat one ingredient.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: これはなんですか。

dialogue.speaker: server
dialogue.ja: えびのサラダです。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: すみません。えびのアレルギーがあります。たべられません。
dialogue.en: Excuse me. I'm allergic to shrimp. I can't eat it.

listenCheck.question: What ingredient can the traveller not eat?

responsePractice.prompt: For a real allergy, state the specific food and show a written allergy card.
choices: [たべもの] のアレルギーがあります。たべられません。
[たべもの] はどこですか。
responsePractice.why: This states the named allergy, but this short phrase is not a safety guarantee. For a real allergy, show a specific written allergy card, ask staff to check ingredients and cross-contact risk, and do not eat unless it is confirmed safe.

lessons.sayTask: Practise saying one real or pretend food limitation clearly; have a partner repeat what they understood.
lessons.adaptation: Ask for another recommendation after explaining the limitation.
successChecks: Catches the ingredient in a reply
Asks for or accepts an alternative

weeks.title: Find places and follow directions
weeks.canDo: Ask where a place is and follow a short direction with one or two turns.

phraseBank.ja: えきはどこですか。
まっすぐいってください。
phraseBank.use: Understand or give a simple direction.

phraseBank.ja: みぎにまがってください。
ここからちかいですか。

kanaFocus: Katakana: voiced marks ガ・ザ・ダ・バ・パ
Katakana: small ャ・ュ・ョ combinations
Read useful signs: ホテル・トイレ・コンビニ

kanjiCards.whyHere: Immediate practical value on buildings and transit signs.

lessons.title: Ask for the station
lessons.goal: Ask for the nearest station and recognize 駅 on a sign.
lessons.scene: You are outside and need to find the nearest station.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: すみません。えきはどこですか。
dialogue.en: Excuse me. Where is the station?

dialogue.speaker: local
dialogue.ja: あのしんごうのところです。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: ありがとうございます。

listenCheck.question: What landmark is near the station?

responsePractice.prompt: Ask where the hotel is.
choices: ホテルはいくらですか。

lessons.sayTask: Ask for the station, hotel, or restroom. Listen for a place or landmark in reply.
lessons.adaptation: Change the destination and ask whether it is near.

lessons.title: Follow two directions
lessons.goal: Follow two short direction steps and confirm their order.
lessons.scene: A passer-by gives a short route to a convenience store.

dialogue.speaker: local
dialogue.ja: まっすぐいってください。

dialogue.speaker: local
dialogue.ja: それから、みぎにまがってください。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: まっすぐいって、みぎですね。

choices: まっすぐいって、みぎですね。

lessons.title: Clarify the destination
lessons.goal: Distinguish an entrance from an exit and clarify which way to go.
lessons.scene: You see both an entrance and an exit and need to know which way to go.

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: すみません。いりぐちはどこですか。
dialogue.en: Excuse me. Where is the entrance?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.ja: でぐちのとなりです。

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: でぐちのとなりですね。

listenCheck.question: Where is the entrance?

responsePractice.prompt: Ask where the exit is.
choices: でぐちはなんじですか。
でぐちはいくらですか。
responsePractice.why: どこですか asks for a place.

weeks.title: Make a time and travel plan
weeks.canDo: Ask what time something starts, agree on a simple meeting time, and confirm how long a trip takes.

phraseBank.ja: なんじですか。
さんじにあいましょう。
どのくらいかかりますか。
もういちどかくにんします。

kanaFocus: Katakana long-vowel mark ー in times and place names
Review numbers and time expressions in spoken phrases

kanjiCards.whyHere: Recognize it in schedules and simple travel information.
Helps read a time on a sign or timetable.

milestone.title: Directions and plans checkpoint
milestone.task: Ask for and confirm a simple direction or meeting time. Extract at least three of four route or time details from a short clear dialogue.

lessons.title: Catch the meeting time

responsePractice.prompt: Suggest meeting at three.

lessons.title: Reconfirm a plan

responsePractice.prompt: Confirm both the time and meeting place.

lessons.sayTask: Listen for day, time, and meeting point; repeat all three details back.
lessons.adaptation: Ask for one detail again if it was unclear, then complete the plan.

weeks.title: Tell a short travel story
weeks.canDo: Describe a simple sequence of what you did or will do, and understand the main events in a brief account.

phraseBank.ja: きょう、[ばしょ] にいきます。

とてもたのしかったです。

lessons.title: Understand a simple plan

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.ja: いいですね。

choices: きょう、ホテルにいきます。
ホテルはいくらですか。

lessons.sayTask: Say one place you are going to today and one question you could ask about it.
lessons.adaptation: Change the place and add when you plan to go.

lessons.title: Tell what happened first

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: きのう、なにをしましたか。

dialogue.speaker: friend
dialogue.ja: どうでしたか。

listenCheck.question: Where did the traveller go?

responsePractice.prompt: Answer a question about an activity you did yesterday.
responsePractice.why: This gives a simple past-tense answer with a place.

lessons.sayTask: Say one thing you did yesterday; a real or imagined example is fine.
lessons.adaptation: Add a reaction, such as たのしかったです or おいしかったです.

lessons.title: Put two events in order

dialogue.speaker: travellerB

lessons.adaptation: Retell it with the events in a new order or add one detail from a follow-up question.

weeks.title: Explain a problem and get help
weeks.canDo: Describe one simple travel problem, ask for help, and repair a misunderstanding.

phraseBank.ja: たすけてください。
さいふをなくしました。
もういちどおねがいできますか。

Revisit katakana signs and names
Practise hearing repair phrases as one chunk

kanjiCards.whyHere: A practical place to recognize when seeking help; learn the whole sign with its reading.

milestone.title: Repair and help checkpoint
milestone.task: Describe a simple problem, ask for clarification or repetition, and continue the exchange. Recognize the main issue and requested help in two short scenarios.
evidence: Repair phrase used and next target

lessons.title: Ask for help at a station

lessons.sayTask: Ask for help and name a simple problem; use a real or imagined situation.
lessons.adaptation: Change the problem to a lost ticket or a missed train.

lessons.title: Explain what is missing

lessons.title: Repair and continue

dialogue.speaker: traveller
dialogue.ja: すみません。もういちどおねがいできますか。

dialogue.speaker: helper

dialogue.ja: ひだりですね。ありがとうございます。

lessons.title: Connect a request and a follow-up

milestone.title: Integrated conversation checkpoint
milestone.task: Sustain a roughly three-minute familiar travel role-play across at least three functions, ask two follow-ups, and use one clarification or repair phrase. After a 45–60 second clear beginner dialogue, state its gist and at least four of five key details.
evidence: Support used and next learning goal
rubric: Gets the main communicative intent across
Uses an appropriate phrase for the situation
Responds to a follow-up or changed detail
Uses clarification or repair when needed
Understands gist and key facts from clear beginner input
